nodes.label: smith-core crate
nodes.rationale: Defines traits and knows nothing about HTTP, SQLite or ratatui; every other crate implements against those traits.

nodes.label: smith-tui crate
nodes.rationale: Never talks to smith-provider or smith-tools directly — only through the Action/AgentEvent channels.

nodes.label: smith-config crate
nodes.rationale: Split out of smith-store so reading a TOML file doesn't compile SQLite from C.

nodes.label: Tool interception pattern
nodes.rationale: Use for any tool whose result depends on interactive UI state rather than pure computation — don't try to make ToolExecutor::execute itself interactive.

nodes.label: Plan gate (plan_gated)
nodes.rationale: Blocks every tool above ReadOnly outright regardless of PermissionPolicy — even Skip doesn't bypass an unapproved plan.

nodes.label: Per-session scratch directory
nodes.rationale: The incentive is the design: a write the tool vouches is scratch-confined skips the permission prompt, so the compliant path is also the frictionless one. Failing closed costs one prompt, never one file.

nodes.label: Tool::scratch_scoped vouching
nodes.rationale: Only write_file/edit_file/multi_edit ever vouch, through one shared fs_tools::scratch_confined; run_bash and MCP tools can never vouch because they cannot bound their writes.

nodes.label: Turn checkpoints (Checkpointer / CheckpointStore)
nodes.rationale: One central hook at the same choke point the plan gate and permission prompt use, so a refused call never leaves an object behind. Deliberately no git and deliberately not in sessions.db: the store has to work with no session row at all.

nodes.label: /rewind
nodes.rationale: Restores files only; it never truncates the conversation. The orchestrator queues Agent::note_to_model, which rides the next user message rather than being a message of its own.

nodes.label: run_bash cannot be snapshotted
nodes.rationale: Any Mutating/Dangerous tool that declares no paths is recorded as uncovered, and /rewind says so rather than implying the turn was fully undone.

nodes.label: Read-before-overwrite gate
nodes.rationale: Checkpoints can undo a blind overwrite, but the user often does not notice until much later, so this prevents rather than undoes. There is no force argument: an escape hatch the model can set itself is not a gate.

nodes.label: fs_tools::ReadSet
nodes.rationale: One Arc shared by read_file/write_file/edit_file/multi_edit; it cannot live on ToolContext (cloned per call) or in a plain registry field (registry is behind an Arc and execute takes &self). Entries are keyed on the sha256 of the bytes read, so a file changed afterwards is stale again.

nodes.label: Behavioral evals (evals/)
nodes.rationale: Out of CI on purpose: a suite that goes red when a provider ships a model update trains people to ignore it.

nodes.label: Headless mode (-p / --output-format)
nodes.rationale: Exit code 3 is distinct from 1 because they warrant opposite reactions in CI — a failure is a bug, a cap is a budget to raise with all prior work intact.

nodes.label: Agent::with_unattended(true)
nodes.rationale: Turns off the two prompt exemptions whose only justification is sparing a human an interruption — scratch-confined writes and task — because both left a call running in a job that named no tools at all.

nodes.label: Free providers and the two-layer fallback
nodes.source_location: ### Free providers and the two-layer fallback
nodes.rationale: Layer one is OpenRouter's server-side chain (models + route:fallback); layer two is FallbackProvider, which on a quota-class death advances a sticky index and returns a retryable error so the agent's existing stream_with_retry drives the next attempt — nothing new retries.

nodes.label: 9Router gateway + private Node provisioning
nodes.rationale: Provisioned into ~/.smith/runtime/ on the Chromium pattern — sha256 vs SHASUMS256.txt, staged, probe-before-rename.

nodes.label: Provider/model switching mid-session (/model)
nodes.rationale: Conversation history carries over either way since messages: Vec<Message> lives independently of the Arc<dyn LlmProvider>.

nodes.label: web_search seven-backend chain
nodes.rationale: A pin is absolute — pinned-but-unconfigured fails naming the missing key rather than silently rerouting, because the user who pins is exactly the user a silent fallback betrays.

nodes.label: SearXNG backend (tier 1)
nodes.rationale: First whenever configured, ahead of even a paid key: it is the only backend with no shared IP reputation and no anti-bot layer. Requires JSON output, which SearXNG ships disabled.

nodes.label: Bing over RSS backend
nodes.rationale: &format=rss returns the same ten results as ~5 KB of stable XML rather than ~122 KB of HTML, with real target URLs instead of Bing's ck/a redirect wrapper. Its <pubDate> is a crawl timestamp, so it is deliberately dropped.

nodes.label: Headless Chromium page fetcher
nodes.rationale: Now a generic page fetcher that knows nothing about result markup — the caller picks the URL and owns the parsing.

nodes.label: language::detect (query-language market selection)
nodes.rationale: A Portuguese query under setmkt=en-US gets ten well-formed results about nothing, structurally indistinguishable from success. The machine locale is the last fallback — WSL2 ships LANG=C.UTF-8, which names no market at all.

nodes.label: bing::judge_relevance (Poisoned / Weak / Good)
nodes.rationale: It grades responses rather than just rejecting them: Poisoned is retried under the next market, Weak is kept as a fallback while a better market gets a try.

nodes.label: Three distinct search-failure cases
nodes.rationale: Collapsing 'found nothing', 'TEMPORARILY BLOCKED' and 'UNAVAILABLE' is what previously ended with the model quietly answering from training data. None of them ever licenses answering from memory.

nodes.label: MCP transports and one liveness rule
nodes.rationale: Transport is the whole abstraction: send one JSON-RPC message, receive on an Incoming channel. The incoming channel closing fails every in-flight call at once, so a server dying mid-session costs no timeouts.

nodes.label: MCP resources are a tool, not context
nodes.rationale: A resource list injected into every request would cost tokens on every turn forever and go stale; a tool is paid for only when used.

nodes.label: MCP prompts are user-invoked, never model-reachable
nodes.rationale: A prompt template is meant to be an instruction, and the only thing that makes that safe is that the user asked for it by name.

nodes.label: untrusted::fence (tool output is DATA)
nodes.rationale: Stated before and after the body, with every run of five hyphens defanged so a payload cannot close the fence. Tool descriptions cannot be fenced, so they get provenance, a 4 KB cap, namespacing and Dangerous.

nodes.label: JSON action envelope (recover_text_tool_call)
nodes.rationale: Only fires when the name resolves to exactly one registered tool: an action field is common enough in ordinary JSON that dispatching on it blindly would turn quoted data into tool calls.

nodes.label: resolve_tool_name / align_arguments
nodes.rationale: Tolerant but never speculative: write against both write_file and write_tasks resolves to nothing rather than to a guess, and edit-distance matching is deliberately absent.

nodes.label: ReasoningFilter
nodes.source_location: ### Reasoning tags in the text channel
nodes.rationale: One shared place inside consume_stream, because the leak follows the model, not the wire format — stripped before deltas are forwarded or accumulated, so nothing reaches the transcript, history or the next request.

nodes.label: Subagents (the task tool)
nodes.rationale: The only thing that crosses back into the parent's history is the child's final message; everything it read is discarded. Measured: six 4 KB reads leave the parent 8074 estimated tokens inline vs 58 when delegated.

nodes.label: subagent::RestrictedTools
nodes.rationale: A child's tool set is the registered ReadOnly tools minus ask_user/write_tasks/task, enforced in code rather than by the prompt.

nodes.label: Shared subagent tool-call pool per turn
nodes.rationale: Per-child caps multiply (50 parent calls x 30 each); a pool is additive, so a turn spends at most twice its own cap.

nodes.label: Partial subagent report (finish_subagent)
nodes.rationale: Throwing partial work away makes the parent re-delegate and pay twice for the half it already had.

nodes.label: Custom slash commands
nodes.rationale: What defuses a prompt from a cloned repo is that the expanded body goes into the transcript as the user's message, above a system line naming the file. A referenced $N with nothing passed refuses the whole expansion rather than expanding to nothing.

nodes.label: Skills (progressive disclosure)
nodes.rationale: A tool rather than a name the model mentions: a tool result is a message so the body invalidates no cached prefix, and it inherits schema validation, permission class, the tool card and stream-json for free.

nodes.label: Personas / output styles
nodes.rationale: Read once at startup and never re-read, so the system prompt is byte-identical for the whole session and prompt caching is untouched.

nodes.label: PROMPT_INVARIANTS vs PROMPT_STYLE split
nodes.rationale: A persona structurally cannot delete the lines that keep output connected to reality, and PROMPT_INVARIANTS stays a byte-identical prefix of every prompt smith sends.

nodes.label: Extension path jail enforced on discovery
nodes.rationale: Nothing in a commands directory says 'read this other file', but .smith/commands/deploy.md -> ~/.ssh/id_rsa is one ln -s in a repository. The jail delegates to memory::real_path because a path jail that exists twice is a path jail that will be fixed once.
